relevance_note: Single case report of a man with a heterozygous ABCA1 splicing variant and probable Tangier disease: 'a novel heterozygous splicing variant in the ABCA1 gene'.
method_note: Read in full by hand; a script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. One proband (label 'patient', rule 5). Relatives in scope as tested (HDL-C lipid screening) family members: youngest brother (HDL-C 35 mg/dL; ABCA1 testing declined), father and mother (both deceased; traced HDL-C 37 and 42 mg/dL, 'both at low to low-normal levels'). The parents' 'low to low-normal' HDL-C is hedged, so low HDL cholesterol is left 'not reported' for them; the brother's HDL-C is not characterised by the authors. The four other siblings declined testing and have no described features, so they get no rows. No relative was genetically tested, so no relative variant rows. Proband: only one ABCA1 allele identified; authors note the second mutation is unidentified and compound heterozygosity cannot be excluded; zygosity recorded as stated (heterozygous). Age at last evaluation left 'not reported': the paper gives 50 years at the 2012 admission but follow-up runs to 2023 without an age. Calculated LDL-C 35 mg/dL and TC 62 mg/dL are given as a 'very good' profile but never called low, so 'low LDL cholesterol' is 'not reported'; small dense LDL is only 'suggested', so not recorded. TG values in Table 1 (56-115 mg/dL) are not characterised; hypertriglyceridemia 'not reported' (only 'severe hypertriglyceridemia' as a secondary cause was 'reasonably excluded', not recorded as a feature). 'his tonsils were not enlarged' excludes enlarged tonsils only, not the composite 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils'. 'Neurological examination was unremarkable with normal sensation and reflexes' and a normal lower-limb nerve conduction study: recorded as excluded abnormal reflexes/sensation/nerve conduction; checklist 'reduced tendon reflexes' and 'reduced deep sensation' excluded from 'normal sensation and reflexes'; 'peripheral neuropathy' left 'not reported' because the paper never names neuropathy for him (whole-exam normal finding, D-27). 'There was no family history of early cardiovascular disease' is not person-specific and was not used. Colonic fatty deposits are described as 'suggestive of' and as 'evidence of fatty deposits'; recorded observed. No contradictions found.
